newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: CYCLONE GILLIAN HOVERS OFF QLD COAST
Far North Queensland is preparing for the possible onslaught of Tropical Cyclone Gillian.
The Category One cyclone is about 420 kilometers east northeast of Cairns and moving south, but is expected to turn towards the coast tonight.
Emergency service and local government counter disaster groups are meeting this morning.

Regional Co-ordinator of the State Emergency Services Department, John Fox says systems are being put in place to advise residents of developments and people are being placed on standby for a recovery phase.
SECURITY IN MELBOURNE FOR TIGER WOODS
Security has been tightened at Melbourne's Huntingdale Golf Course, because of what officials are calling phenominal interest in today's appearance by American golfing star, Tiger Woods.
Woods will tee-off this afternoon in the pro-am, the lead-up event to Thursday's Australian Masters.
The Secretary of the Huntingdale Golf Club, Geoff Brooks says Woods could be responsible for record crowds.
GROCERS UNHAPPY WITH ELECTRONIC BANKING

The accelerating push into electronic banking in Australia has prompted criticism today from sections of the retail sector. The National Association of Retail Grocers of Australia says people are being herded into electronic banking through unwarranted changes to fees and charges.
The Association says retailers are being forced to act as de facto bank tellers.
President Ian Baldock says the Association has argued for some time that banks are shirking their responsibility by forcing retailers to conduct banking business at the retailers' own expense.
BLAKE'S COMPENSATION SLASHED
A multi-million-dollar compensation payment to former film star John Blake has been slashed by the New South Wales Court of Appeal.
The Supreme Court awarded the actor a record 33-million-dollars in 1995 after he was left brain damaged in a car accident in South Australia 11 years ago.
But New South Wales' highest court today upheld an appeal by an insurance company against the damages pay-out.
While the exact amount of the new award has yet to be calculated, the pay-out to the former film star could be halved. - - - -
SPACE TELESCOPE LAUNCH PROBES SECRETS OF BLACK HOLES
Australia will join an international mission investigating black holes in space after the launch of the first space radio telescope in Japan this afternoon.
The CSIRO's Doctor John Reynolds says the first project will be to investigate a black hole in a galaxy 100-million light years away.
He says the mission is trying to get a much clearer picture of how galaxies form.
The joint effort will involve 40 radio telescopes in 17 countries, including six in Australia.
Combining signals from the eight metre space telescope will those on land, will effectively create a radio telescope with a diameter three times larger than the Earth's.
